subject: On-prem VPC schematic: ops risk assessment & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@telcoco.com>, infra@acme.com
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem VPC schematic: ops risk assessment & next steps

Alex / ACME team — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Attached is the latest schematic (v1) we sketched during the call and an initial egress matrix. High level ask: we need your input on two items by EOD Friday so we can lock the canary plan for the on‑prem pilot.

Quick summary of outstanding risk areas from our side:
- Control plane reachability: how will your NOC accept inbound mTLS control connections from our management proxies? Need IP ranges + expected MTLS cert exchange cadence.
- Egress termination: Telcoco wants to centralize egress through a perimeter NAT/IDS — we need exact SNAT ranges for mapping tenant egress.
- BGP vs static: For the tenant-facing data plane, do you want BGP peer sessions or static routes for service IPs? BGP preferred for failover but adds ops overhead.

Immediate requests (actionable):
1) Confirm acceptance of our control-plane management CIDR (10.240.5.0/28) or propose alternate.
2) Attach a contact + SLA for cert rotation / emergency revocation (ops email + runbook link).
3) Flag any compliance controls that would block prefix-level NAT (e.g., PCI/CHIPS egress inspection).

Attachments: vpc_schematic_v1.pdf, egress_matrix.xlsx (stubs attached).

Thanks — I’ll consolidate answers and publish a short runbook draft for the pilot cutover.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Soto <alex.soto@telcoco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@acme.com, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC schematic: ops risk assessment & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the artifacts. Quick answers inline:  

- Control plane reachability: Telcoco NOC will accept mTLS from your management proxies if we have a CA chain and an IP allowlist. 10.240.5.0/28 is fine for initial staging; production will need to move to a /27. We will provide the IP allowlist by Thursday.
- Egress termination: We can centralize egress through our perimeter NAT. For tenant mapping we will allocate a pool per tenant group; we can provide the SNAT ranges as soon as the tenant assignments are final. Note: traffic inspection rules will drop TLS‑intercepted connections unless explicitly exempted.
- BGP vs static: ops prefers BGP for the data plane. We can provision med/local_pref controls for failover. We will need a short test window to validate session flapping behavior.

Attachments: The NOC provided a sample cert rotation SLA (see link below).

Next steps from our side:
1) We’ll upload the IP allowlist and a stub runbook to the shared Drive by Thursday.
2) Assign Alex/Devon as the 24/7 oncall for the pilot cutover.

—
Alex Soto
Infrastructure Lead — Telcoco Communications
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex.soto@telcoco.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC schematic: ops risk assessment & next steps

Alex — great, thanks. Two clarification items:
- Production control-plane /27: can you confirm a tentative schedule for expanding the allowlist? We want to align cert rollovers so there is no window where our management proxies are blocked.
- Inspection exemptions: we’ll need a documented path for exempting mTLS connection metadata from TLS inspection for telemetry and KV cache sync. If inspection is mandatory, we’ll need to move to out-of-band telemetry.

Mina / Irene / Ben — can each of you call out a single blocker from an ops/security perspective so we can publish a clean RACI? Please reply in-thread.

I’ll schedule a 30m sync for Friday afternoon (15:00 PT) to finalize the canary cutover checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Soto <alex.soto@telcoco.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC schematic: ops risk assessment & next steps

Marissa / Alex — from an ops/readiness POV the main blockers I see:  

1) Cert rotation SLAs need concrete emergency revocation steps with a 2-hour window for high-severity incidents. The Telcoco sample is a start but we need commitment in writing before cutover.
2) Egress SNAT pools: we need a mapping document that ties tenant IDs to SNAT ranges to avoid accidental traffic co-mingling during ramp. Prefer a per-tenant /29 allocation for initial pilot.
3) Control-plane telemetry: if inspection blocks our telemetry, we must spin an out-of-band metrics forwarder. That adds ~0.8s p95 to our control sync times; acceptable for warm-up but we need to track impact.

If Telcoco can commit to the above items, I’m comfortable greenlighting the canary (with a rollback hold at hour +3).

—
Mina Haddad
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Alex Soto <alex.soto@telcoco.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem VPC schematic: ops risk assessment & next steps

Looping in acceptance criteria from the customer-facing side — per Telcoco commercial:
- Pilot must not exceed 12 hours of planned user-facing downtime across the cutover window.
- We need a signed acknowledgment of our rollback SLA and an estimate of incident triage times from Telcoco NOC.

Alex — can you confirm the NOC triage SLA & provide the contact for the 24/7 oncall you mentioned? If we have these in place I’ll finalize the mutual action plan and create the HubSpot deal artifact.

Thanks — I’ll post the draft runbook (with play-level rollback steps) to the Drive when Marissa confirms the Friday sync.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
